1731	## H1Density (whole result)
  1732	
  1733	A deterministic foundation of wave L7 (item L7-c), in
  1734	`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/H1Density.lean`: smooth compactly supported
  1735	functions are dense in the weak-gradient `H^1(R^d; R)` of `WeakSobolev`. It
  1736	carries no manuscript label of its own. The manuscript states the fact in one
  1737	sentence in the proof of `P:spatial-four-linear`
  1738	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at revision `975feb3`, proposition
  1739	lines 149-167, proof lines 169-228; the density sentence and its sketch are
  1740	lines 192-196) and uses it to extend smooth-profile statements to `H^1`
  1741	profiles: in the same proof at lines 200-201 ("take smooth approximants
  1742	converging in `H^1`") and line 220, and in the proof of `P:spatial-energy-map`
  1743	(lines 257-276) at lines 258-260 and 269. Every hypothesis is stated; nothing
  1744	is supplied. In the completion module `SpatialOccupationL7Completed` it
  1745	discharges the density hypothesis `hdense` of `SpatialFourLinear`
  1746	(`P:spatial-four-linear` and `P:spatial-energy-map`).
  1747	
  1748	- The space is the package's own `H^1` (Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces):
  1749	  `WeakSobolev.IsTestFunction` (`C_c^infinity(R^d; R)`),
  1750	  `WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient f g` (`int f d_v phi = -int <g, v> phi` for
  1751	  every test function `phi` and direction `v`) and `WeakSobolev.MemH1`
  1752	  (`f` in `L^2` with a weak gradient in `L^2`); the gradient of a smooth
  1753	  function is the classical field `VariationalFloor.grad`. The approximation
  1754	  is in the graph norm: `norm(phi_n - f)_2 -> 0` and
  1755	  `norm(grad phi_n - g)_2 -> 0`, which is convergence in the TeX's `H^1`
  1756	  norm.
  1757	- `H1TestDense d` is the predicate (its body is fixed for the consumers of
  1758	  wave L7); `h1TestDense d` proves it for every `d`, including `d = 0`, which
  1759	  is more than the manuscript's `d = 1, 2, 3`. `exists_test_approx` is the
  1760	  `eps` form and `h1TestDense_of_memH1` the `MemH1` form.
  1761	- `hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto` is the converse (an `L^2` graph limit of test
  1762	  functions has the limit gradient as weak gradient), so the weak-gradient
  1763	  `H^1` is the closure of `C_c^infinity` in the graph norm. The manuscript
  1764	  does not state it; it is used by the refutation `DropWeakGradient`.
  1765	- Lean proof route (different from the TeX in order and in the
  1766	  mollification step). (1) Mollify first: `mollify phi u = rho_phi * u` with
  1767	  the normalized bump `rho_phi = phi.normed volume`; the `L^2` contraction
  1768	  `eLpNorm_mollify_le` (Cauchy-Schwarz against the probability weight, then
  1769	  Tonelli and translation invariance) and the density of continuous compactly
  1770	  supported functions in `L^2` give `rho_n * u -> u` in `L^2` when the bump
  1771	  radii tend to `0` (`tendsto_mollify`), where the TeX invokes `L^2`
  1772	  translation continuity; the weak-gradient identity tested against
  1773	  `y -> rho_phi(x - y)` gives `grad(rho_phi * f) = rho_phi * g`
  1774	  (`grad_mollify`). (2) Then cut off the smooth function `h = rho * f` with
  1775	  `chi_n(x) = chi(x/(n+1))`, `chi = 1` on the closed unit ball and `0` outside
  1776	  the ball of radius `2`; the classical product rule (`grad_cutoff_mul`),
  1777	  dominated convergence (`tendsto_cutoff_smul`) and
  1778	  `norm(h grad chi_n)_2 <= C norm(h)_2/(n+1)` (`norm_grad_cutoff_le`) give
  1779	  `tendsto_cutoff_test`. This is the cutoff estimate of TeX lines 192-195
  1780	  with `R = n + 1`, applied after mollification to a smooth function, so no
  1781	  weak product rule is needed. (3) An `eps/2` argument and `eps = 1/(k+1)`
  1782	  give the sequence. The mollifiers are `VariationalFloor.bumpN` (so
  1783	  `mollify (VariationalFloor.bumpN d n) f` is `VariationalFloor.moll f n` by
  1784	  definition, for real `f`).
  1785	- Not formalized: the separability remark of the same proof (lines 196-198),
  1786	  and the "common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e." of lines 200-201 (the density
  1787	  gives `L^2` convergence only; an a.e.-convergent subsequence is a separate
  1788	  step for the consumer).
  1789	- Junk values: none relied on. In the density statements `f` and `g` are in
  1790	  `L^2`, so the integrals in `HasWeakGradient` against test functions are
  1791	  genuine; all norms are `eLpNorm` values in `[0, infinity]`.
  1792	
  1793	Refutations (`refutations/h1-density/`): `DropMemLpF` (drop `f in L^2`: the
  1794	constant `1` in `d = 1`, weak gradient `0`, is not an `L^2` limit of test
  1795	functions), `DropWeakGradient` (drop the weak-gradient hypothesis:
  1796	`f = 0`, `g = prof e_0` in `d = 1`, via `hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto` and
  1797	`WeakSobolev.weakGradient_ae_unique`), `NotTestFunction` (every `H^1`
  1798	function a test function: the indicator of the origin in `d = 1`), and
  1799	`ContractionConstant` (the contraction with constant `1/2`, refuted at
  1800	`u = VariationalFloor.prof` in `d = 1` by `tendsto_mollify`). No junk-value
  1801	reliance. Lemmas labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof
  1802	route)" serve only the Lean proofs and are not TeX steps.

  1978	## IntervalScalar (whole result)
  1979	
  1980	Formalizes the deterministic scalar, combinatorial and Hilbert-space steps of
  1981	two results of `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `975feb3`:
  1982	`C:static-interaction` (statement lines 2612-2658, proof 2660-2723) and
  1983	`P:interval-coefficients` (statement lines 3329-3341, proof 3343-3508). Both
  1984	results are operator and stochastic statements; every row below is a step row
  1985	(class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement), except
  1986	`E:static-block-series`, which is a scalar statement and is proved in full with
  1987	nothing supplied (`static_block_series_paper`). The operator and stochastic
  1988	inputs enter as named hypotheses; the last column names each one with its
  1989	manuscript label.
  1990	
  1991	`C:static-interaction`. `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)` is modelled by an arbitrary
  1992	complete real inner product space `E`, and the transported phases
  1993	`Y_n = S_0(-h) Z_n^eps(h)` by a sequence `Y : N -> E`; the expectation of an
  1994	inner product is the inner product of `E`. This is faithful because the proof
  1995	of `E:static-interaction` (lines 2660-2697) uses only the Hilbert structure:
  1996	the order bounds of lines 2673-2678, the Gaussian parity of line 2679, and
  1997	the two first-variance bounds of lines 2664-2669. Those are the supplied
  1998	hypotheses `hY0`, `hY`, `hodd`, `hborn`, `hmean`. The identification of
  1999	`I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g)` with `sum sigma^n Y_n` (lines 2614-2619) is not
  2000	formalized. Lean proves that `sum sigma^n Y_n` converges and the bound
  2001	`(1 + E(h, sigma, lambda)) N^2`. `L_alpha`, `B_alpha`, `x` and `E` are the
  2002	definitions `staticL`, `staticB`, `staticX`, `staticE`, word for word; `A`
  2003	stands for `A_alpha` and may be any constant `>= 0`. The section's constants
  2004	are `R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` and `D_Gamma` of
  2005	`E:phase-constants` (lines 1985-1992), for locally finite `mu`, `Gamma` on
  2006	`R^3` and `0 < alpha < 2`. These are the only clauses of the TeX's covariance
  2007	class (line 1981) in the wrappers. Evenness, positive definiteness and scaling
  2008	enter only through the supplied hypotheses. `R_alpha >= 0` and `D_Gamma >= 0`
  2009	are derived (`ralpha_nonneg`, `dgamma_nonneg`). The `_step` and
  2010	`static_block_series` forms take them as hypotheses. The TeX argues with the
  2011	absolutely convergent double series; Lean bounds the partial sums, regrouped
  2012	by `r + s = 2k` (`square_sum_eq`), keeps the first coefficient signed, and
  2013	passes to the limit. For `E:independent-static-blocks`, Lean proves the scalar
  2014	iteration and `1 + y <= e^y`. The per-block bound
  2015	`m_(j+1) <= e^(lambda h_j)(1 + E) m_j` is supplied (lines 2714-2720: it uses
  2016	`E:static-interaction`, `\|S_0(h_j)\|^2 <= e^(lambda h_j)`, density and
  2017	tensoring with the independent past). The operators `M_j(h_j)` and their
  2018	`L^2` extensions are not formalized. Hypotheses carried but unused: `0 < alpha`
  2019	in `static_interaction_step`; `0 < alpha` in `static_block_series` (its
  2020	`0 < alpha0` is used: with `alpha + alpha0 < 2` it gives `alpha < 2`); local finiteness of `mu`, `Gamma` (it only makes the
  2021	ball masses finite, so that `toReal` is not a junk value); `lambda h_j <= 1` in
  2022	`independent_static_blocks_paper`.
  2023	
  2024	`P:interval-coefficients`. The energy coefficient `[s^(2k)] E\|U(T;s)v\|^2`,
  2025	the split inner products `Q_(r,q)` and `\|v\|_(1/T)^2` are real numbers `coef`,
  2026	`Q p`, `V`. Colors are `j : Fin M` with the TeX's sorted label `i = j + 1`.
  2027	Supplied hypotheses:
  2028	- `hsplits`: `E:interval-energy-splits` combined with the reflection parity
  2029	  (lines 3405-3415).
  2030	- `hfixed`: `L:fixed-split` (`E:fixed-split-bound`; lemma lines 2980-3021) at
  2031	  `lambda = k/T`. Its per-color factor is `splitFactor`, with `l_i` as
  2032	  `splitEll`.
  2033	- `hinv`: `L:inventory-product` as the proposition `InventoryProduct alpha
  2034	  alpha0 C_inv` (lines 2913-2925). Proved in `InventoryProduct`
  2035	  (`inventory_product`) and discharged in `IntervalScalarCompleted`, whose
  2036	  `*_completed` forms do not take it. Lean formalizes the rest of the assembly
  2037	  (lines 3426-3474): the length substitution `h_i <= L T/i` at `lambda = k/T`,
  2038	  `sigma_i^2 <= c h_i^(-alpha0)` (`singleton_weight_le`, `cross_weight_le`,
  2039	  `higher_weight_le`); the split count `2l + 1 <= 3^l`; `k^2 <= 4^k`; the
  2040	  coefficient-of-a-product identity (`kvector_sum_eq_coeff`); and the
  2041	  reduction `L -> max(1, L)`, `c -> max(c, 0)` (lines 3344-3347). Together
  2042	  these give the explicit constant `C = 12 max(c,0) max(1,L)^beta C_split
  2043	  C_inv`. The paper wrapper assumes `R_alpha > 0` and `sigma_i > 0`, the
  2044	  hypotheses of `L:fixed-split`, so that `hfixed` is literally that lemma.
  2045	  Neither is used in the proof. The TeX's zero-noise case and the sign
  2046	  reduction `(sigma_i, W_i) -> (|sigma_i|, sgn(sigma_i) W_i)` (lines 3344,
  2047	  3347-3350) change the Gaussian fields and are not formalized, so the
  2048	  conclusion is narrower there. Positive lengths `h_i > 0` are explicit (the
  2049	  TeX writes `h_i^(-alpha0)`). The identification of the coefficients with the
  2050	  finite-interval model is not formalized: the Hermite cutoff (lines
  2051	  3417-3424) and the paragraph "Identification and summation" (lines
  2052	  3476-3493). For `E:interval-phase-bound` (lines 3494-3506), Lean proves
  2053	  summability of the coefficient series and the bound `e exp(nu C^(1/nu)
  2054	  R_alpha^(1/nu) T^(beta/nu)) V`, the TeX's display with its absorbed constant
  2055	  `nu C^(1/nu)`, from four supplied hypotheses:
  2056	- the power-series identity at `s = 1`;
  2057	- vanishing odd coefficients;
  2058	- the zero-order bound `e V`;
  2059	- the coefficient bound.
  2060	Both wrappers state the section's class as `H:homog`
  2061	(`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, line 190; the section's standing
  2062	class at lines 2741-2746 is that of `H:homog`), from which `0 < alpha < 2`,
  2063	`0 < alpha0 < 1` and `alpha + alpha0 < 2` are derived (`homog_alpha_range`);
  2064	the other clauses are carried and not used.
  2065	
  2066	Junk values: in the manuscript-facing bounds every real power has a positive
  2067	base, or is `(k!)^nu`, or is `i^q` with `i >= 1` (or a nonnegative base with a
  2068	positive exponent where monotonicity is used), and every denominator satisfies
  2069	the stated positivity conditions. The unrestricted definitions (`invV`, `invB`,
  2070	`invCoeff`) and the bridge identities of `IntervalScalarCompleted` (stated for
  2071	all `k, i`) also include Lean's totalized zero-index values, which no bound
  2072	uses. `R_alpha` and `D_Gamma` use `ENNReal.toReal` of ball
  2073	masses, finite under local finiteness. Summability is proved, never assumed
  2074	through `tsum`.

    69	theorem norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg (v : ℕ → E) (S : E) (hS : HasSum v S)

    83	    le_hasSum (hcol n) n (fun k _ => hpos n k)
    84	  have h2 : inner ℝ (v n) S ≤ inner ℝ S S :=

    94	theorem term_bound (Y : ℕ → E) (r B : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r)
    95	    (hsum : Summable fun n => ‖r ^ n • Y n‖)
    96	    (hpos : ∀ m n, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (Y m) (Y n))
    97	    (hB : ‖∑' n, r ^ n • Y n‖ ^ 2 ≤ B) (n : ℕ) :

   101	  have hpos' : ∀ m k, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (r ^ m • Y m) (r ^ k • Y k) := by

   108	  have h' : r ^ n * ‖Y n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B := by

    74	/-! ### The objects of `L:inventory-product` -/
    75	
    76	/-- `p = 2 - α₀` (main TeX line 2739). `ν = 3 - α` and `β = 4 - α - α₀`
    77	(lines 2738-2739) are `TypeContinuity.nuOf` and `TypeContinuity.betaOf`. -/
    78	def pOf (alpha0 : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 - alpha0
    79	
    80	/-- `v_i = i^{-β} + k^{-1} i^{-(β-1)} + k^{α-2} i^{-p}` (main TeX lines 2916-2917). -/
    81	def vCoef (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (k i : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    82	  (i : ℝ) ^ (-betaOf alpha alpha0) + (k : ℝ)⁻¹ * (i : ℝ) ^ (-(betaOf alpha alpha0 - 1)) +
    83	    (k : ℝ) ^ (alpha - 2) * (i : ℝ) ^ (-pOf alpha0)
    84	
    85	/-- `b_{i,l} = i^{-βl}(1 + li/k)^2/(l!)^ν` (main TeX line 2918). -/
    86	def bCoef (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (k i l : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    87	  (i : ℝ) ^ (-betaOf alpha alpha0 * l) * (1 + l * i / k) ^ 2 / ((l ! : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ nuOf alpha
    88	
    89	/-- The coefficients of the `i`th factor `1 + v_i z + ∑_{l ≥ 2} b_{i,l} z^l`. -/
    90	def factorCoeff (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (k i l : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    91	  if l = 0 then 1 else if l = 1 then vCoef alpha alpha0 k i else bCoef alpha alpha0 k i l
    92	
    93	/-- The `i`th factor as a formal power series. -/
    94	def factorSeries (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (k i : ℕ) : PowerSeries ℝ :=
    95	  PowerSeries.mk (factorCoeff alpha alpha0 k i)

    98	`E:inventory-product` (main TeX lines 2921-2925), as a formal power series. -/
    99	def inventoryProduct (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (M k : ℕ) : PowerSeries ℝ :=
   100	  ∏ i ∈ Icc 1 M, factorSeries alpha alpha0 k i

   103	def factorEval (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (k i : ℕ) (z : ℝ) : ℝ :=

   261	    have hai := ht i hi
   262	    rw [mem_image]
   263	    exact ⟨i - a - 1, by rw [mem_range]; omega, by omega⟩

   457	/-- Auxiliary: the exponent `g_i` of the bound `F_i(θ k^ν) ≤ e^{g_i}`; for

   462	  1 / 4 * (k : ℝ) * (i : ℝ) ^ (-pOf alpha0) +
   463	    if i ≤ k then nuOf alpha * k * (i : ℝ) ^ (-(betaOf alpha alpha0 / nuOf alpha))

   466	      8 * (k : ℝ) ^ (2 * nuOf alpha) * (i : ℝ) ^ (-(2 * betaOf alpha alpha0)) +
   467	      8 * (k : ℝ) ^ (2 * nuOf alpha - 2) * (i : ℝ) ^ (-(2 * betaOf alpha alpha0 - 2))

   162	      rw [ENNReal.zero_rpow_of_pos (by norm_num)] at h2
   163	      exact h2
   164	  rw [lintegral_zero] at hL
   165	  have h2 := ((ENNReal.continuous_rpow_const (y := 1 / (2 : ℝ))).tendsto 0).comp hL
   166	  rw [ENNReal.zero_rpow_of_pos (by norm_num)] at h2
   167	  exact h2

   169	/-! ### Mollification -/
   170	
   171	section Mollify
   172	
   173	variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
   174	
   175	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the mollification
   176	`ρ_φ ⋆ u (x) = ∫ ρ_φ(t) u(x - t) dt` with the normalized bump
   177	`ρ_φ = φ.normed volume` (nonnegative, integral `1`, support the ball of
   178	radius `φ.rOut`), for real- or vector-valued `u`. -/
   179	def mollify (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) (u : Rd d → F) : Rd d → F :=
   180	  convolution (φ.normed volume) u (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume
   181	
   182	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the mollification of a locally
   183	integrable function is continuous. -/
   184	theorem continuous_mollify (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) {u : Rd d → F}
   185	    (hu : LocallyIntegrable u volume) : Continuous (mollify φ u) :=
   186	  φ.hasCompactSupport_normed.continuous_convolution_left _
   187	    (φ.continuous_normed (μ := volume)) hu
   188	
   189	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the mollification of a locally
   190	integrable function is smooth. -/
   191	theorem contDiff_mollify (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) {u : Rd d → F}
   192	    (hu : LocallyIntegrable u volume) : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (mollify φ u) :=
   193	  φ.hasCompactSupport_normed.contDiff_convolution_left _ φ.contDiff_normed hu
   194	
   195	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the `L²` contraction
   196	`‖ρ_φ ⋆ u‖₂ ≤ ‖u‖₂` (Cauchy-Schwarz against the probability weight `ρ_φ`,
   197	then Tonelli and translation invariance). -/
   198	theorem eLpNorm_mollify_le (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) {u : Rd d → F}
   199	    (hu : MemLp u 2 volume) :
   200	    eLpNorm (mollify φ u) 2 volume ≤ eLpNorm u 2 volume := by
   201	  set ρ : Rd d → ℝ := φ.normed volume with hρ
   202	  set a : Rd d → ℝ≥0∞ := fun t => ENNReal.ofReal (ρ t) with ha
   203	  have ham : Measurable a := (φ.continuous_normed (μ := volume)).measurable.ennreal_ofReal
   204	  have ha1 : ∫⁻ t, a t = 1 := by
   205	    rw [ha, ← ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal φ.integrable_normed
   206	      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun t => φ.nonneg_normed t), φ.integral_normed,
   207	      ENNReal.ofReal_one]
   208	  have hloc : LocallyIntegrable u volume := hu.locallyIntegrable (by norm_num)
   209	  have hpt : ∀ x, ‖mollify φ u x‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) ≤ ∫⁻ t, a t * ‖u (x - t)‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) := by
   210	    intro x
   211	    have h1 : ‖mollify φ u x‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ t, a t * ‖u (x - t)‖ₑ := by
   212	      rw [mollify, convolution_def]
   213	      refine (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm _).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
   214	      congr 1; funext t
   215	      rw [ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply, enorm_smul, Real.enorm_eq_ofReal (φ.nonneg_normed t)]
   216	    have hbm : AEMeasurable (fun t => ‖u (x - t)‖ₑ) volume :=
   217	      hu.aestronglyMeasurable.enorm.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving
   218	        (quasiMeasurePreserving_sub_left_of_right_invariant volume x)
   219	    exact (ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow h1 (by norm_num)).trans
   220	      (lintegral_mul_sq_le volume ham.aemeasurable hbm ha1)
   221	  have hprod : AEMeasurable (Function.uncurry fun x t => a t * ‖u (x - t)‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ))
   222	      ((volume : Measure (Rd d)).prod volume) := by
   223	    have hb : AEMeasurable (fun p : Rd d × Rd d => ‖u (p.1 - p.2)‖ₑ)
   224	        ((volume : Measure (Rd d)).prod volume) :=
   225	      hu.aestronglyMeasurable.enorm.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving
   226	        (quasiMeasurePreserving_sub_of_right_invariant volume volume)
   227	    exact (ham.comp measurable_snd).aemeasurable.mul (hb.pow_const _)
   228	  have hint : ∫⁻ x, ‖mollify φ u x‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) ≤ ∫⁻ x, ‖u x‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) := by
   229	    calc _ ≤ ∫⁻ x, ∫⁻ t, a t * ‖u (x - t)‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) := lintegral_mono hpt
   230	      _ = ∫⁻ t, ∫⁻ x, a t * ‖u (x - t)‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) := lintegral_lintegral_swap hprod
   231	      _ = ∫⁻ t, a t * ∫⁻ x, ‖u x‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) := by
   232	        congr 1; funext t
   233	        have hm : AEMeasurable (fun x => ‖u (x - t)‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ)) volume :=
   234	          (hu.aestronglyMeasurable.enorm.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving
   235	            ((measurePreserving_sub_right volume t).quasiMeasurePreserving)).pow_const _
   236	        rw [lintegral_const_mul'' _ hm]
   237	        rw [lintegral_sub_right_eq_self (fun x => ‖u x‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ)) t]
   238	      _ = ∫⁻ x, ‖u x‖ₑ ^ (2 : ℝ) := by
   239	        rw [lintegral_mul_const _ ham, ha1, one_mul]
   240	  rw [eLpNorm_eq_lintegral_rpow_enorm_toReal (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   241	      (continuous_mollify φ hloc).aestronglyMeasurable,
   242	    eLpNorm_eq_lintegral_rpow_enorm_toReal (by norm_num) (by norm_num) hu.aestronglyMeasurable]
   243	  rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofNat]
   244	  exact ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow hint (by norm_num)
   245	
   246	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the mollification of an `L²`
   247	function is in `L²`. -/
   248	theorem memLp_mollify (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) {u : Rd d → F}
   249	    (hu : MemLp u 2 volume) : MemLp (mollify φ u) 2 volume :=
   250	  memLp_iff.mpr (lt_of_le_of_lt (eLpNorm_mollify_le φ hu) hu.eLpNorm_lt_top)
   251	
   252	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: mollification is additive on
   253	differences of locally integrable functions. -/
   254	theorem mollify_sub (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) {u w : Rd d → F}
   255	    (hu : LocallyIntegrable u volume) (hw : LocallyIntegrable w volume) (x : Rd d) :
   256	    mollify φ u x - mollify φ w x = mollify φ (fun y => u y - w y) x := by
   257	  have eu := (φ.hasCompactSupport_normed.convolutionExists_left
   258	    (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) (φ.continuous_normed (μ := volume)) hu x).integrable
   259	  have ew := (φ.hasCompactSupport_normed.convolutionExists_left
   260	    (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) (φ.continuous_normed (μ := volume)) hw x).integrable
   261	  simp only [mollify, convolution_def]
   262	  rw [← integral_sub eu ew]
   263	  congr 1; funext t
   264	  simp [smul_sub]
   265	
   266	variable [CompleteSpace F]
   267	
   268	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: for a continuous compactly
   269	supported `c` with values in a complete space, `ρ_n ⋆ c → c` in `L²` when
   270	the bump radii tend to `0` (uniform convergence on a fixed compact set). -/
   271	theorem tendsto_mollify_of_continuous {c : Rd d → F} (hc : Continuous c)
   272	    (hcs : HasCompactSupport c) {φ : ℕ → ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)}
   273	    (hφ : Tendsto (fun n => (φ n).rOut) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
   274	    Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => mollify (φ n) c x - c x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   275	  set K : Set (Rd d) := Metric.closedBall (0 : Rd d) 1 + tsupport c with hK
   276	  have hKc : IsCompact K := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : Rd d) 1).add hcs
   277	  have hM : (volume K) ^ (1 / (2 : ℝ≥0∞).toReal) ≠ ⊤ :=
   278	    ENNReal.rpow_ne_top_of_nonneg (by norm_num) hKc.measure_lt_top.ne
   279	  refine tendsto_zero_of_eventually_le hM fun η hη => ?_
   280	  obtain ⟨δ, hδ, hδc⟩ := Metric.uniformContinuous_iff.mp
   281	    (hcs.uniformContinuous_of_continuous hc) η hη
   282	  filter_upwards [hφ.eventually (gt_mem_nhds (lt_min hδ one_pos))] with n hn
   283	  have hn' := lt_min_iff.mp hn
   284	  have hloc : LocallyIntegrable c volume := hc.locallyIntegrable
   285	  refine eLpNorm_sub_le_of_dist_bdd volume (by norm_num)
   286	    hKc.isClosed.measurableSet.nullMeasurableSet hη.le
   287	    ((continuous_mollify (φ n) hloc).sub hc).aestronglyMeasurable ?_ ?_ ?_
   288	  · intro x
   289	    refine (φ n).dist_normed_convolution_le hc.aestronglyMeasurable fun y hy => ?_
   290	    exact (hδc (lt_trans (Metric.mem_ball.mp hy) hn'.1)).le
   291	  · refine (support_convolution_subset _).trans ?_
   292	    rw [(φ n).support_normed_eq]
   293	    exact Set.add_subset_add (Metric.ball_subset_closedBall.trans
   294	      (Metric.closedBall_subset_closedBall hn'.2.le)) (subset_tsupport c)
   295	  · exact (subset_tsupport c).trans fun x hx => ⟨0, Metric.mem_closedBall_self zero_le_one, x,
   296	      hx, zero_add x⟩
   297	
   298	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (in place of the TeX's `L²`
   299	translation continuity): for `u ∈ L²` with values in a complete space,
   300	`ρ_n ⋆ u → u` in `L²` when the bump radii `(φ n).rOut` tend to `0`. -/
   301	theorem tendsto_mollify {u : Rd d → F} (hu : MemLp u 2 volume)
   302	    {φ : ℕ → ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)} (hφ : Tendsto (fun n => (φ n).rOut) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
   303	    Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => mollify (φ n) u x - u x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   304	  rw [ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero]
   305	  intro ε hε
   306	  obtain ⟨c, hcs, hcε, hc, hcL⟩ := hu.exists_hasCompactSupport_eLpNorm_sub_le (by norm_num)
   307	    (ENNReal.div_pos hε.ne' (by norm_num : (3 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ⊤)).ne'
   308	  have hloc : LocallyIntegrable u volume := hu.locallyIntegrable (by norm_num)
   309	  have hlocc : LocallyIntegrable c volume := hc.locallyIntegrable
   310	  filter_upwards [(ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero.mp (tendsto_mollify_of_continuous hc hcs hφ))
   311	    (ε / 3) (ENNReal.div_pos hε.ne' (by norm_num : (3 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ⊤))] with n hn
   312	  have hA : eLpNorm (fun x => mollify (φ n) u x - mollify (φ n) c x) 2 volume ≤ ε / 3 := by
   313	    simp_rw [mollify_sub (φ n) hloc hlocc]
   314	    exact (eLpNorm_mollify_le (φ n) (hu.sub hcL)).trans hcε
   315	  have hsplit : (fun x => mollify (φ n) u x - u x) =
   316	      ((fun x => mollify (φ n) u x - mollify (φ n) c x) + fun x => mollify (φ n) c x - c x) +
   317	        fun x => c x - u x := by
   318	    funext x; simp only [Pi.add_apply]; abel
   319	  have hcu : eLpNorm (fun x => c x - u x) 2 volume ≤ ε / 3 := by
   320	    rw [show (fun x => c x - u x) = c - u from rfl, eLpNorm_sub_comm]; exact hcε
   321	  rw [hsplit]
   322	  calc _ ≤ eLpNorm ((fun x => mollify (φ n) u x - mollify (φ n) c x) +
   323	          fun x => mollify (φ n) c x - c x) 2 volume + eLpNorm (fun x => c x - u x) 2 volume :=
   324	        eLpNorm_add_le (by norm_num)
   325	    _ ≤ (eLpNorm (fun x => mollify (φ n) u x - mollify (φ n) c x) 2 volume +
   326	          eLpNorm (fun x => mollify (φ n) c x - c x) 2 volume) +
   327	          eLpNorm (fun x => c x - u x) 2 volume := by
   328	        gcongr; exact eLpNorm_add_le (by norm_num)
   329	    _ ≤ ε / 3 + ε / 3 + ε / 3 := by gcongr
   330	    _ = ε := ENNReal.add_thirds ε
   331	
   332	end Mollify
   333	
   334	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: if `g` is a weak gradient of the
   335	locally integrable `f` (with `g` locally integrable), the derivative of

336	`ρ_φ ⋆ f` in the direction `v` is `⟪ρ_φ ⋆ g, v⟫`: the weak-gradient identity
   337	tested against the test function `y ↦ ρ_φ(x - y)`. -/
   338	theorem fderiv_mollify_apply (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   339	    (hf : LocallyIntegrable f volume) (hg : LocallyIntegrable g volume)
   340	    (h : HasWeakGradient f g) (x v : Rd d) :
   341	    fderiv ℝ (mollify φ f) x v = inner ℝ (mollify φ g x) v := by
   342	  set ρ : Rd d → ℝ := φ.normed volume with hρ
   343	  have hρs : HasCompactSupport ρ := φ.hasCompactSupport_normed
   344	  have hρc : ContDiff ℝ ∞ ρ := φ.contDiff_normed
   345	  have hρ1 : ContDiff ℝ 1 ρ := hρc.of_le (by exact_mod_cast le_top)
   346	  have hD : HasFDerivAt (mollify φ f)
   347	      (convolution (fderiv ℝ ρ) f (ContinuousLinearMap.precompL (Rd d)
   348	        (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ)) volume x) x :=
   349	    hρs.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left _ hρ1 hf x
   350	  have hex := (hρs.fderiv ℝ).convolutionExists_left
   351	    (ContinuousLinearMap.precompL (Rd d) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ (E := ℝ)))
   352	    (hρc.continuous_fderiv (by simp)) hf x
   353	  rw [hD.fderiv, convolution_def, ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply hex v]
   354	  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.precompL_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
   355	  rw [← integral_sub_left_eq_self _ volume x]
   356	  simp only [sub_sub_cancel]
   357	  set ψ : Rd d → ℝ := fun s => ρ (x - s) with hψ
   358	  have hψt : IsTestFunction ψ := by
   359	    refine ⟨hρc.comp (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id), ?_⟩
   360	    exact hρs.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.subLeft x)
   361	  have hψd : ∀ s, fderiv ℝ ψ s v = -(fderiv ℝ ρ (x - s) v) := by
   362	    intro s
   363	    have h1 : HasFDerivAt (fun s => x - s) (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Rd d)) s :=
   364	      (hasFDerivAt_id s).const_sub x
   365	    have h2 := ((hρc.differentiable (by simp)) (x - s)).hasFDerivAt.comp s h1
   366	    rw [show ψ = ρ ∘ fun s => x - s from rfl, h2.fderiv]
   367	    simp
   368	  have hw := h ψ hψt v
   369	  simp only [hψd, mul_neg, integral_neg, neg_inj] at hw
   370	  have hexg := (φ.hasCompactSupport_normed.convolutionExists_left
   371	    (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) (φ.continuous_normed (μ := volume)) hg x).integrable
   372	  have hR : inner ℝ (mollify φ g x) v = ∫ s, inner ℝ (g s) v * ψ s := by
   373	    rw [mollify, convolution_def, real_inner_comm, ← integral_inner hexg v]
   374	    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply, real_inner_smul_right]
   375	    rw [← integral_sub_left_eq_self _ volume x]
   376	    simp only [sub_sub_cancel]
   377	    congr 1; funext s; rw [hψ, real_inner_comm, mul_comm]
   378	  have e1 : (∫ s, fderiv ℝ ρ (x - s) v * f s) = ∫ s, f s * fderiv ℝ ρ (x - s) v := by
   379	    congr 1; funext s; ring
   380	  rw [hR, e1, hw]
   381	
   382	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the classical gradient of a
   383	mollified function is the mollified weak gradient, `∇(ρ_φ ⋆ f) = ρ_φ ⋆ g`,
   384	for locally integrable `f, g` with `HasWeakGradient f g`. -/
   385	theorem grad_mollify (φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d)) {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   386	    (hf : LocallyIntegrable f volume) (hg : LocallyIntegrable g volume)
   387	    (h : HasWeakGradient f g) : grad (mollify φ f) = mollify φ g := by
   388	  funext x
   389	  rw [grad, LinearIsometryEquiv.symm_apply_eq]
   390	  ext v
   391	  rw [fderiv_mollify_apply φ hf hg h x v, InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply]
   392	
   393	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the radii `2/(n+2)` of
   394	`VariationalFloor.bumpN` tend to `0`. -/
   395	theorem tendsto_bumpN_rOut : Tendsto (fun n => (bumpN d n).rOut) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   396	  show Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) / (n + 2)) atTop (𝓝 0)
   397	  have h := tendsto_const_div_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (2 : ℝ)
   398	  refine (h.comp (tendsto_add_atTop_nat 2)).congr' ?_
   399	  filter_upwards with n; simp [Nat.cast_add]
   400	
   401	/-! ### Cutoff -/
   402	
   403	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the cutoff profile `χ`, equal to `1`
   404	on the closed unit ball and `0` outside the open ball of radius `2`. -/
   405	def cutBump (d : ℕ) : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d) := ⟨1, 2, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩
   406	
   407	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the cutoff `χ_n(x) = χ(x/(n+1))`
   408	(TeX line 192-193 with `R = n + 1`). -/
   409	def cutoff (n : ℕ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ := cutBump d (((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • x)
   410	
   411	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `χ_n` is smooth. -/
   412	theorem cutoff_contDiff (n : ℕ) : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (cutoff (d := d) n) :=
   413	  (cutBump d).contDiff.comp (contDiff_const_smul _)
   414	
   415	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `χ_n` has compact support. -/
   416	theorem cutoff_hasCompactSupport (n : ℕ) : HasCompactSupport (cutoff (d := d) n) :=
   417	  (cutBump d).hasCompactSupport.comp_smul (inv_ne_zero (by positivity))
   418	
   419	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `0 ≤ χ_n`. -/
   420	theorem cutoff_nonneg (n : ℕ) (x : Rd d) : 0 ≤ cutoff n x := (cutBump d).nonneg
   421	
   422	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `χ_n ≤ 1`. -/
   423	theorem cutoff_le_one (n : ℕ) (x : Rd d) : cutoff n x ≤ 1 := (cutBump d).le_one
   424	
   425	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `χ_n = 1` on the ball of radius
   426	`n + 1`. -/
   427	theorem cutoff_eq_one {n : ℕ} {x : Rd d} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ (n : ℝ) + 1) : cutoff n x = 1 := by
   428	  refine (cutBump d).one_of_mem_closedBall ?_
   429	  rw [Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, norm_smul, norm_inv, Real.norm_eq_abs,
   430	    abs_of_pos (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) + 1)]
   431	  show ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ * ‖x‖ ≤ 1
   432	  rw [inv_mul_le_iff₀ (by positivity)]; simpa using hx
   433	
   434	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `χ_n h` is a test function for
   435	every smooth `h`. -/
   436	theorem cutoff_isTest (n : ℕ) {h : Rd d → ℝ} (hh : ContDiff ℝ ∞ h) :
   437	    IsTestFunction (fun x => cutoff n x * h x) :=
   438	  ⟨(cutoff_contDiff n).mul hh, (cutoff_hasCompactSupport n).mul_right⟩
   439	
   440	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the classical product rule
   441	`∇(χ_n h) = χ_n ∇h + h ∇χ_n` for smooth `h`. -/
   442	theorem grad_cutoff_mul (n : ℕ) {h : Rd d → ℝ} (hh : ContDiff ℝ ∞ h) (x : Rd d) :
   443	    grad (fun x => cutoff n x * h x) x = cutoff n x • grad h x + h x • grad (cutoff n) x := by
   444	  have h1 : DifferentiableAt ℝ (cutoff (d := d) n) x :=
   445	    ((cutoff_contDiff n).differentiable (by simp)) x
   446	  have h2 : DifferentiableAt ℝ h x := (hh.differentiable (by simp)) x
   447	  simp only [grad]
   448	  rw [fderiv_fun_mul h1 h2, map_add, map_smul, map_smul]
   449	
   450	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `‖Dχ‖` is bounded. -/
   451	theorem exists_bound_fderiv_cutBump :
   452	    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ y : Rd d, ‖fderiv ℝ (cutBump d) y‖ ≤ C := by
   453	  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := ((cutBump d).hasCompactSupport.fderiv ℝ).exists_bound_of_continuous
   454	    (((cutBump d).contDiff (n := 1)).continuous_fderiv one_ne_zero)
   455	  exact ⟨max C 0, le_max_right _ _, fun y => (hC y).trans (le_max_left _ _)⟩
   456	
   457	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `‖∇χ_n‖ ≤ C/(n+1)` when `‖Dχ‖ ≤ C`
   458	(the TeX's gradient bound `C/R`, line 193). -/
   459	theorem norm_grad_cutoff_le {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ y : Rd d, ‖fderiv ℝ (cutBump d) y‖ ≤ C)
   460	    (n : ℕ) (x : Rd d) : ‖grad (cutoff n) x‖ ≤ C / ((n : ℝ) + 1) := by
   461	  simp only [grad, LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map]

   515	  rw [hsplit]

   523	/-! ### Density -/
   524	
   525	/-- Density in `ε` form: for `f, g ∈ L²` with `g` a weak gradient of `f`
   526	and every `ε > 0` there is a test function `ψ` with `‖ψ - f‖₂ ≤ ε` and
   527	`‖∇ψ - g‖₂ ≤ ε`.  (Lean proof route: mollify, then cut off; see the module
   528	doc comment.) -/
   529	theorem exists_test_approx {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d} (hf : MemLp f 2 volume)
   530	    (hg : MemLp g 2 volume) (hw : HasWeakGradient f g) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : 0 < ε) :
   531	    ∃ ψ : Rd d → ℝ, IsTestFunction ψ ∧
   532	      eLpNorm (fun x => ψ x - f x) 2 volume ≤ ε ∧
   533	      eLpNorm (fun x => grad ψ x - g x) 2 volume ≤ ε := by
   534	  have hε2 : 0 < ε / 2 := ENNReal.div_pos hε.ne' (by norm_num)
   535	  have hfl : LocallyIntegrable f volume := hf.locallyIntegrable (by norm_num)
   536	  have hgl : LocallyIntegrable g volume := hg.locallyIntegrable (by norm_num)
   537	  have T1 := ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero.mp (tendsto_mollify hf (tendsto_bumpN_rOut (d := d)))
   538	    (ε / 2) hε2
   539	  have T2 := ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero.mp (tendsto_mollify hg (tendsto_bumpN_rOut (d := d)))
   540	    (ε / 2) hε2
   541	  obtain ⟨N, hN1, hN2⟩ := (T1.and T2).exists
   542	  set h : Rd d → ℝ := mollify (bumpN d N) f with hhdef
   543	  have hh : ContDiff ℝ ∞ h := contDiff_mollify _ hfl
   544	  have hgrad : grad h = mollify (bumpN d N) g := grad_mollify _ hfl hgl hw
   545	  have hL : MemLp h 2 volume := memLp_mollify _ hf
   546	  have hG : MemLp (grad h) 2 volume := hgrad ▸ memLp_mollify _ hg
   547	  obtain ⟨C1, C2⟩ := tendsto_cutoff_test hh hL hG
   548	  obtain ⟨n, hn1, hn2⟩ :=
   549	    ((ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero.mp C1 (ε / 2) hε2).and
   550	      (ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero.mp C2 (ε / 2) hε2)).exists
   551	  refine ⟨fun x => cutoff n x * h x, cutoff_isTest n hh, ?_, ?_⟩
   552	  · have hs : (fun x => cutoff n x * h x - f x) =
   553	        (fun x => cutoff n x * h x - h x) + fun x => h x - f x := by
   554	      funext x; simp only [Pi.add_apply]; ring
   555	    rw [hs]
   556	    calc _ ≤ _ := eLpNorm_add_le (by norm_num)
   557	      _ ≤ ε / 2 + ε / 2 := add_le_add hn1 hN1
   558	      _ = ε := ENNReal.add_halves ε
   559	  · have hs : (fun x => grad (fun y => cutoff n y * h y) x - g x) =
   560	        (fun x => grad (fun y => cutoff n y * h y) x - grad h x) + fun x => grad h x - g x := by
   561	      funext x; simp only [Pi.add_apply]; abel
   562	    rw [hs]
   563	    calc _ ≤ _ := eLpNorm_add_le (by norm_num)
   564	      _ ≤ ε / 2 + ε / 2 := by
   565	        refine add_le_add hn2 ?_
   566	        rw [hgrad]; exact hN2
   567	      _ = ε := ENNReal.add_halves ε

   569	/-- **Density of `C_c^∞` in the weak-gradient `H^1`** (half (a) of the
   570	D8-lite foundation; `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex`, proof of
   571	`P:spatial-four-linear`, lines 192-196 at 975feb3), for every dimension `d`.
   572	Lean proof route: mollification first (with an `L²` contraction and density
   573	of `C_c` in `L²` in place of the TeX's translation continuity), then the
   574	TeX's cutoff estimate; see the module doc comment. -/
   575	theorem h1TestDense (d : ℕ) : H1TestDense d := by
   576	  intro f g hf hg hw
   577	  have hpos : ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < ENNReal.ofReal (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) := fun k =>
   578	    ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr (by positivity)
   579	  choose φ hφt hφ1 hφ2 using fun k : ℕ => exists_test_approx hf hg hw (hpos k)
   580	  have hT : Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => ENNReal.ofReal (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1))) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   581	    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_zero]
   582	    exact ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat
   583	  exact ⟨φ, hφt,
   584	    tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds hT (fun _ => zero_le) hφ1,
   585	    tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds hT (fun _ => zero_le) hφ2⟩
   586	
   587	/-- The `MemH1` form of the density: every `f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)` has an `L²`
   588	weak gradient `g` and test functions `φ_n` with `φ_n → f` and `∇φ_n → g` in
   589	`L²`. -/
   590	theorem h1TestDense_of_memH1 {f : Rd d → ℝ} (hf : MemH1 f) :
   591	    ∃ g : Rd d → Rd d, MemLp g 2 volume ∧ HasWeakGradient f g ∧
   592	      ∃ φ : ℕ → Rd d → ℝ, (∀ n, IsTestFunction (φ n)) ∧
   593	        Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => φ n x - f x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
   594	        Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => grad (φ n) x - g x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   595	  obtain ⟨hfL, g, hg, hw⟩ := hf
   596	  exact ⟨g, hg, hw, h1TestDense d f g hfL hg hw⟩
   597	
   598	/-! ### The converse: limits of test functions -/
   599	
   600	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route of `hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto`: if
   601	`u n → u₀` in `L²` (all in `L²`) and `w ∈ L²`, then `∫ u n w → ∫ u₀ w`
   602	(Hölder with exponents `2, 2, 1`). -/
   603	theorem tendsto_integral_mul_of_L2 {u : ℕ → Rd d → ℝ} {u0 w : Rd d → ℝ}
   604	    (hu : ∀ n, MemLp (u n) 2 volume) (hu0 : MemLp u0 2 volume) (hw : MemLp w 2 volume)
   605	    (hT : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => u n x - u0 x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
   606	    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, u n x * w x) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, u0 x * w x)) := by
   607	  refine tendsto_integral_of_L1 (fun x => u0 x * w x)
   608	    (hu0.aestronglyMeasurable.mul hw.aestronglyMeasurable)
   609	    (Eventually.of_forall fun n => (hu n).integrable_mul hw) ?_
   610	  have hB : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => u n x - u0 x) 2 volume * eLpNorm w 2 volume)
   611	      atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   612	    simpa using ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const hT (Or.inr hw.eLpNorm_lt_top.ne)
   613	  refine tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds hB
   614	    (fun _ => zero_le) (fun n => ?_)
   615	  have hm : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => u n x - u0 x) volume :=
   616	    (hu n).aestronglyMeasurable.sub hu0.aestronglyMeasurable
   617	  have e : (fun x => ‖u n x * w x - u0 x * w x‖ₑ) =
   618	      fun x => ‖((fun x => u n x - u0 x) • w) x‖ₑ := by
   619	    funext x
   620	    show ‖u n x * w x - u0 x * w x‖ₑ = ‖(u n x - u0 x) * w x‖ₑ
   621	    rw [sub_mul]
   622	  calc ∫⁻ x, ‖u n x * w x - u0 x * w x‖ₑ
   623	      = eLpNorm ((fun x => u n x - u0 x) • w) 1 volume := by
   624	        rw [e, eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm (hm.smul hw.aestronglyMeasurable)]
   625	    _ ≤ _ := eLpNorm_smul_le_mul_eLpNorm hm hw.aestronglyMeasurable
   626	
   627	/-- The converse of the density (closedness of the weak gradient under
   628	`L²` limits of test functions): if test functions `φ n` satisfy `φ n → f` and
   629	`∇φ n → g` in `L²`, with `f, g ∈ L²`, then `g` is a weak gradient of `f`.
   630	Together with `h1TestDense` this identifies the weak-gradient `H^1` with the
   631	closure of `C_c^∞` under the norm `‖f‖₂ + ‖∇f‖₂`. -/
   632	theorem hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   633	    (hf : MemLp f 2 volume) (hg : MemLp g 2 volume) {φ : ℕ → Rd d → ℝ}
   634	    (hφ : ∀ n, IsTestFunction (φ n))
   635	    (h1 : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => φ n x - f x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0))
   636	    (h2 : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => grad (φ n) x - g x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
   637	    HasWeakGradient f g := by
   638	  intro ψ hψ v
   639	  have hinner : ∀ G : Rd d → Rd d, MemLp G 2 volume →
   640	      MemLp (fun x => inner ℝ (G x) v) 2 volume := by
   641	    intro G hG
   642	    refine ((innerSL ℝ v).comp_memLp' hG).congr_norm hG.aestronglyMeasurable.inner_const
   643	      (Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
   644	    simp [real_inner_comm]
   645	  have hwv : MemLp (fun x => fderiv ℝ ψ x v) 2 volume := by
   646	    refine ((hψ.1.continuous_fderiv (by simp)).clm_apply
   647	      continuous_const).memLp_of_hasCompactSupport ?_
   648	    exact (hψ.2.fderiv ℝ).comp_left (g := fun L : Rd d →L[ℝ] ℝ => L v) (by simp)
   649	  have A := tendsto_integral_mul_of_L2 (fun n => VariationalFloor.memLp_test (hφ n)) hf hwv h1
   650	  have hB : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => inner ℝ (grad (φ n) x) v - inner ℝ (g x) v) 2
   651	      volume) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   652	    have hM : Tendsto (fun n => ENNReal.ofReal ‖v‖ *
   653	        eLpNorm (fun x => grad (φ n) x - g x) 2 volume) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   654	      have := ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul h2 (Or.inr (ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top (r := ‖v‖)))
   655	      rwa [mul_zero] at this
   656	    refine tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds hM
   657	      (fun _ => zero_le) (fun n => ?_)
   658	    refine eLpNorm_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_ae_le_mul ?_ (Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_) 2
   659	    · exact ((hinner _ (VariationalFloor.memLp_grad (hφ n))).sub
   660	        (hinner _ hg)).aestronglyMeasurable
   661	    · rw [← inner_sub_left, mul_comm]
   662	      exact (Real.norm_eq_abs _).trans_le (abs_real_inner_le_norm _ _)

   664	    (fun n => hinner _ (VariationalFloor.memLp_grad (hφ n)))
   665	    (hinner _ hg) (VariationalFloor.memLp_test hψ) hB

   668	    refine B.neg.congr fun n => ?_

   670	  exact tendsto_nhds_unique A A'

    68	positive semidefiniteness of `B_Γ` on smooth signed profiles from the spectral identity; smooth
    69	covariance Cauchy-Schwarz; Fatou along a.e.-convergent subsequences of the density
    70	approximants (`squareBound_of_smooth`); Cauchy-Schwarz under `ν` for `E:spatial-four-linear`;
    71	telescoping for continuity.  Differences: `E:spatial-square-CS` on `H¹` passes the smooth
    72	inequality `B_Γ(φ²,ψ²)² ≤ A_sp(φ)A_sp(ψ)` to the limit by continuity of `C₄` (the TeX passes
    73	positive semidefiniteness to combinations of `H¹` squares); `b > 0` on unit profiles by
    74	`VariationalFloor.ae_eq_zero_of_hasWeakGradient_zero` (mollification) instead of the Fourier
    75	support argument; positivity of `A_sp` uses a compact set and Mathlib's continuity of the
    76	measure of translates instead of `L²` translation continuity of `1_E`; for
    77	`E:spatial-energy-map` the upper bound applies `E:spatial-homogeneous-bound` and weighted AM-GM
    78	to every unit profile and the lower bound dilates smooth unit tests only (the TeX extends the
    79	dilation to `H¹`); scores are obtained by continuity of the scalar maps along smooth ratios
    80	increasing to `R_0`.
    81	
    82	Narrower than the TeX (recorded): joint continuity of `C₄` is stated sequentially for `H¹`
    83	convergence of the pairs (equivalent to continuity for the `H¹` seminorm topology); continuity
    84	of `A_sp` and the square pairings is not restated separately (they are `C₄(f,f,f,f)` and
    85	`C₄(f,f,h,h)` by `pairing_toReal_eq_C4`); `E:spatial-static-energy-score` is in the existential
    86	form, and in the `sSup` form only on `S1Bdd`.  Lemmas marked "Auxiliary to the Lean proof
    87	route" have no manuscript label.  Both propositions are in this one module; the fallback scope
    88	was not needed.

   118	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the cross-correlation `y ↦ ∫ F(x) G(x-y) dx` (the inner
   119	integral of `B_Γ(F,G)`) is the convolution `F ⋆ G(-·)`. -/
   120	theorem cross_eq_convolution (F G : Rd d → ℝ) :
   121	    (fun y => ∫ x, F x * G (x - y)) =
   122	      convolution F (fun x => G (-x)) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume := by
   123	  funext y
   124	  simp only [convolution, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply, smul_eq_mul, neg_sub]
   125	
   126	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: for continuous compactly supported `F, G` and locally finite
   127	`Γ`, the cross-correlation is `Γ`-integrable (it is continuous with compact support). -/
   128	theorem cross_integrable (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ] {F G : Rd d → ℝ}
   129	    (hF : Continuous F) (hFs : HasCompactSupport F) (hG : Continuous G)
   130	    (hGs : HasCompactSupport G) : Integrable (fun y => ∫ x, F x * G (x - y)) Γ := by
   131	  rw [cross_eq_convolution]
   132	  refine Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport ?_ ?_
   133	  · exact (hGs.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.neg _)).continuous_convolution_right
   134	      (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) hF.locallyIntegrable (hG.comp continuous_neg)
   135	  · exact hFs.convolution (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) (hGs.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.neg _))
   136	
   137	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: for continuous `F` with compact support and continuous `G`,
   138	`x ↦ F(x) G(x-y)` is integrable for every `y`. -/
   139	theorem inner_integrable {F G : Rd d → ℝ} (hF : Continuous F) (hFs : HasCompactSupport F)
   140	    (hG : Continuous G) (y : Rd d) : Integrable (fun x => F x * G (x - y)) volume :=
   141	  (hF.mul (hG.comp (continuous_id.sub continuous_const))).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
   142	    hFs.mul_right
   143	
   144	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: bilinear expansion of the real pairing `B_Γ(Q+tP, Q+tP)` for
   145	continuous compactly supported `Q, P` and locally finite `Γ` (TeX lines 184-185, "the quadratic
   146	polynomial for `Q+tP`"). -/
   147	theorem spatialPair_quad (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ] {Q P : Rd d → ℝ}
   148	    (hQ : Continuous Q) (hQs : HasCompactSupport Q) (hP : Continuous P)
   149	    (hPs : HasCompactSupport P) (t : ℝ) :
   150	    spatialPair Γ (fun x => Q x + t * P x) (fun x => Q x + t * P x) =
   151	      spatialPair Γ Q Q + t * (spatialPair Γ Q P + spatialPair Γ P Q) +
   152	        t ^ 2 * spatialPair Γ P P := by
   153	  have hin : ∀ y, ∫ x, (Q x + t * P x) * (Q (x - y) + t * P (x - y)) =
   154	      (∫ x, Q x * Q (x - y)) + (t * ((∫ x, Q x * P (x - y)) + ∫ x, P x * Q (x - y)) +
   155	        t ^ 2 * ∫ x, P x * P (x - y)) := by
   156	    intro y
   157	    have i1 := inner_integrable hQ hQs hQ y
   158	    have i2 := inner_integrable hQ hQs hP y
   159	    have i3 := inner_integrable hP hPs hQ y
   160	    have i4 := inner_integrable hP hPs hP y
   161	    have e : (fun x => (Q x + t * P x) * (Q (x - y) + t * P (x - y))) = fun x =>
   162	        Q x * Q (x - y) + (t * (Q x * P (x - y) + P x * Q (x - y)) +
   163	          t ^ 2 * (P x * P (x - y))) := by
   164	      funext x; ring
   165	    have k2 : Integrable (fun x => t * (Q x * P (x - y) + P x * Q (x - y))) volume :=
   166	      (i2.add i3).const_mul t
   167	    have k3 : Integrable (fun x => t ^ 2 * (P x * P (x - y))) volume := i4.const_mul _
   168	    have k1 : Integrable (fun x => t * (Q x * P (x - y) + P x * Q (x - y)) +
   169	        t ^ 2 * (P x * P (x - y))) volume := k2.add k3
   170	    rw [e, integral_add i1 k1, integral_add k2 k3, integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul,
   171	      integral_add i2 i3]
   172	  have j1 := cross_integrable Γ hQ hQs hQ hQs
   173	  have j2 := cross_integrable Γ hQ hQs hP hPs
   174	  have j3 := cross_integrable Γ hP hPs hQ hQs
   175	  have j4 := cross_integrable Γ hP hPs hP hPs
   176	  unfold spatialPair
   177	  simp_rw [hin]
   178	  have k2 : Integrable (fun y => t * ((∫ x, Q x * P (x - y)) + ∫ x, P x * Q (x - y))) Γ :=
   179	    (j2.add j3).const_mul t
   180	  have k3 : Integrable (fun y => t ^ 2 * ∫ x, P x * P (x - y)) Γ := j4.const_mul _
   181	  have k1 : Integrable (fun y => t * ((∫ x, Q x * P (x - y)) + ∫ x, P x * Q (x - y)) +
   182	      t ^ 2 * ∫ x, P x * P (x - y)) Γ := k2.add k3
   183	  rw [integral_add j1 k1, integral_add k2 k3, integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul,
   184	    integral_add j2 j3]
   185	  ring

   187	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: symmetry `B_Γ(Q,P) = B_Γ(P,Q)` for an even `Γ`
   188	(`HomogHypothesis.IsEven`), continuous `P, Q` and compactly supported `Q` (TeX lines 183-184:
   189	evenness of `Γ` and `(x,y) ↦ (x-y,-y)`; Lean route: translation `x ↦ x + y` and the pushforward
   190	under `y ↦ -y`). -/
   191	theorem spatialPair_comm {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hE : IsEven Γ) {Q P : Rd d → ℝ}
   192	    (hP : Continuous P) (hQ : Continuous Q) (hQs : HasCompactSupport Q) :
   193	    spatialPair Γ Q P = spatialPair Γ P Q := by
   194	  have hin : ∀ y, ∫ x, Q x * P (x - y) = (fun z => ∫ x, P x * Q (x - z)) (-y) := by
   195	    intro y
   196	    rw [← integral_add_right_eq_self (fun x => Q x * P (x - y)) y]
   197	    simp only [add_sub_cancel_right, sub_neg_eq_add]
   198	    congr 1; funext x; ring
   199	  have hc : Continuous fun z => ∫ x, P x * Q (x - z) := by
   200	    rw [cross_eq_convolution]
   201	    exact (hQs.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.neg _)).continuous_convolution_right
   202	      (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) hP.locallyIntegrable (hQ.comp continuous_neg)
   203	  unfold spatialPair
   204	  simp_rw [hin]
   205	  have hm := integral_map (μ := Γ) (φ := fun x : Rd d => -x) measurable_neg.aemeasurable
   206	    (f := fun z => ∫ x, P x * Q (x - z)) hc.aestronglyMeasurable
   207	  have hE' : Γ.map (fun x : Rd d => -x) = Γ := hE
   208	  rw [hE'] at hm
   209	  exact hm.symm

   211	/-- Smooth signed covariance is positive (TeX lines 175-181): for real `Q ∈ C_c^∞` and a spectral
   212	measure `μ` of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention, `B_Γ(Q,Q) = ∫ |Q̂|² dμ ≥ 0`
   213	(`SpatialFourierBound.integral_autocorr_eq_spectral`).  As a Bochner-integral statement; for
   214	locally finite `Γ` the integrand is integrable (`SpatialFourierBound.integrable_autocorr`). -/
   215	theorem spatialPair_self_nonneg {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ)
   216	    {Q : Rd d → ℝ} (hQ : IsTestFunction Q) : 0 ≤ spatialPair Γ Q Q := by
   217	  show 0 ≤ ∫ y, autocorr Q y ∂Γ
   218	  rw [SpatialFourierBound.integral_autocorr_eq_spectral hsp hQ.1 hQ.2]
   219	  exact integral_nonneg fun _ => by positivity
   220	
   221	/-- Covariance Cauchy-Schwarz on smooth profiles (TeX lines 184-186): for real `Q, P ∈ C_c^∞`, a
   222	locally finite even `Γ` with spectral measure `μ`, `B_Γ(Q,P)² ≤ B_Γ(Q,Q) B_Γ(P,P)` (discriminant
   223	of `t ↦ B_Γ(Q+tP,Q+tP) ≥ 0`). -/
   224	theorem spatialPair_sq_le {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ] (hE : IsEven Γ)
   225	    (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) {Q P : Rd d → ℝ} (hQ : IsTestFunction Q)
   226	    (hP : IsTestFunction P) :
   227	    spatialPair Γ Q P ^ 2 ≤ spatialPair Γ Q Q * spatialPair Γ P P := by
   228	  have hq : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ spatialPair Γ P P * (t * t) + 2 * spatialPair Γ Q P * t +
   229	      spatialPair Γ Q Q := by
   230	    intro t
   231	    have hT : IsTestFunction fun x => Q x + t * P x :=
   232	      ⟨hQ.1.add (contDiff_const.mul hP.1), hQ.2.add hP.2.mul_left⟩
   233	    have h := spatialPair_self_nonneg hsp hT
   234	    rw [spatialPair_quad Γ hQ.1.continuous hQ.2 hP.1.continuous hP.2,
   235	      spatialPair_comm hE hQ.1.continuous hP.1.continuous hP.2] at h
   236	    nlinarith [h]
   237	  have := discrim_le_zero hq
   238	  unfold discrim at this
   239	  nlinarith [this]

   242	
   243	/-- `‖f‖₂ = (eLpNorm f 2).toReal`, the `L²` norm as a real number (`0` if `f ∉ L²`; it is used only
   244	on `L²` functions). -/
   245	def l2 {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (f : Rd d → E) : ℝ :=
   246	  (eLpNorm f 2 volume).toReal
   247	
   248	/-- `N(f) = ‖f‖₂^{1-α/4} ‖∇f‖₂^{α/4}` (TeX line 151), with `∇f` given as an `L²` weak gradient `g`
   249	of `f` (a.e. unique, `WeakSobolev.weakGradient_ae_unique`). -/
   250	def Nnorm (alpha : ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : ℝ :=
   251	  l2 f ^ (1 - alpha / 4) * l2 g ^ (alpha / 4)
   252	
   253	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `‖f‖₂ ≥ 0`. -/
   254	theorem l2_nonneg {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (f : Rd d → E) : 0 ≤ l2 f :=
   255	  ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
   256	
   257	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `N(f) ≥ 0`. -/
   258	theorem Nnorm_nonneg (alpha : ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : 0 ≤ Nnorm alpha f g :=
   259	  mul_nonneg (rpow_nonneg (l2_nonneg _) _) (rpow_nonneg (l2_nonneg _) _)
   260	
   261	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: for `f ∈ L²`, `‖f‖₂² = ∫ ‖f‖²`. -/
   262	theorem l2_sq {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {f : Rd d → E} (hf : MemLp f 2 volume) :
   263	    l2 f ^ 2 = ∫ x, ‖f x‖ ^ 2 := by
   264	  unfold l2
   265	  rw [hf.eLpNorm_eq_integral_rpow_norm (by norm_num) (by norm_num)]
   266	  simp only [ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, rpow_two]
   267	  have h0 : 0 ≤ ∫ x, ‖f x‖ ^ 2 := integral_nonneg fun _ => by positivity
   268	  rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (rpow_nonneg h0 _), ← rpow_natCast, ← rpow_mul h0]
   269	  norm_num
   270	
   271	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `N(f)⁴ = (‖f‖₂²)^{(4-α)/2} (‖g‖₂²)^{α/2}` (no hypotheses:
   272	`‖·‖₂ ≥ 0`). -/
   273	theorem Nnorm_pow_four (alpha : ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) :
   274	    Nnorm alpha f g ^ 4 = (l2 f ^ 2) ^ ((4 - alpha) / 2) * (l2 g ^ 2) ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   275	  have h1 := l2_nonneg f
   276	  have h2 := l2_nonneg g
   277	  unfold Nnorm
   278	  rw [mul_pow, ← rpow_natCast, ← rpow_natCast (l2 g ^ (alpha / 4)), ← rpow_mul h1,
   279	    ← rpow_mul h2, ← rpow_natCast (l2 f) 2, ← rpow_natCast (l2 g) 2, ← rpow_mul h1,
   280	    ← rpow_mul h2]
   281	  congr 2 <;> push_cast <;> ring

   288	    gradEnergy φ = l2 (grad φ) ^ 2 := by

   314	  have e : (fun x => (c * g x) ^ 2) = fun x => c ^ 2 * g x ^ 2 := by funext x; ring

   322	
   323	/-- `E:spatial-homogeneous-bound` for smooth compact profiles (TeX lines 170-171, "normalization in
   324	`R_0`", including `f = 0`): if every real unit test `g` has `A_sp(g) ≤ R b(g)^{α/2}`, then every
   325	`φ ∈ C_c^∞` has `A_sp(φ) ≤ R N(φ)⁴`, with `N` computed from the classical gradient.  Hypothesis
   326	`α < 4`. -/
   327	theorem smooth_homog_bound {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} {alpha R : ℝ} (ha4 : alpha < 4)
   328	    (hR : ∀ g, IsUnitTest g → spatialEnergy Γ g ≤ R * gradEnergy g ^ (alpha / 2))
   329	    {φ : Rd d → ℝ} (hφ : IsTestFunction φ) :
   330	    spatialEnergy Γ φ ≤ R * Nnorm alpha φ (grad φ) ^ 4 := by
   331	  rw [Nnorm_pow_four, ← integral_sq_eq_l2_sq (VariationalFloor.memLp_test hφ),
   332	    ← gradEnergy_eq_l2_sq hφ]
   333	  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ : ∃ m, m = ∫ x, φ x ^ 2 := ⟨_, rfl⟩
   334	  rw [← hm]
   335	  have hm0 : 0 ≤ m := by rw [hm]; exact integral_nonneg fun x => sq_nonneg (φ x)
   336	  rcases hm0.eq_or_lt with h | h
   337	  · have hi : Integrable (fun x => φ x ^ 2) volume :=
   338	      (isTest_sq hφ).1.continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport (isTest_sq hφ).2
   339	    have hae : (fun x => φ x ^ 2) =ᵐ[volume] 0 :=
   340	      (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun x => sq_nonneg (φ x)) hi).1 (h.trans hm).symm
   341	    have h2 : (fun x => φ x ^ 2) = 0 :=
   342	      (Continuous.ae_eq_iff_eq volume (hφ.1.continuous.pow 2) continuous_zero).1 hae
   343	    have hz : φ = 0 := funext fun x => by
   344	      have := congr_fun h2 x
   345	      simpa using this
   346	    rw [← h, zero_rpow (by linarith : (4 - alpha) / 2 ≠ 0), zero_mul, mul_zero]
   347	    subst hz
   348	    simp [spatialEnergy, spatialPair]
   349	  · have hc2 : (Real.sqrt m)⁻¹ ^ 2 = m⁻¹ := by rw [inv_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hm0]
   350	    have hc4 : (Real.sqrt m)⁻¹ ^ 4 = m⁻¹ ^ 2 := by

351	      rw [show (4 : ℕ) = 2 * 2 from rfl, pow_mul, hc2]
   352	    have hg : IsUnitTest fun x => (Real.sqrt m)⁻¹ * φ x := by
   353	      refine ⟨contDiff_const.mul hφ.1, hφ.2.mul_left, ?_⟩
   354	      simp_rw [mul_pow, hc2]
   355	      rw [integral_const_mul, ← hm, inv_mul_cancel₀ h.ne']
   356	    have h1 := hR _ hg
   357	    rw [spatialEnergy_const_mul, gradEnergy_const_mul (hφ.1.differentiable (by simp)), hc4,
   358	      hc2] at h1
   359	    have hG0 : 0 ≤ gradEnergy φ := SpatialFourierBound.gradEnergy_nonneg φ
   360	    have hma : 0 < m ^ (alpha / 2) := rpow_pos_of_pos h _

   362	        (m ^ (alpha / 2))⁻¹ * gradEnergy φ ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   363	      rw [mul_rpow (inv_nonneg.2 hm0) hG0, inv_rpow hm0]
   364	    have e2 : m ^ ((4 - alpha) / 2) = m ^ 2 / m ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   365	      rw [show (4 - alpha) / 2 = (2 : ℝ) - alpha / 2 by ring, rpow_sub h, rpow_two]
   366	    rw [e1] at h1
   367	    rw [e2]
   368	    have hm2 : 0 < m ^ 2 := by positivity
   369	    calc spatialEnergy Γ φ = m ^ 2 * (m⁻¹ ^ 2 * spatialEnergy Γ φ) := by
   370	          field_simp
   371	      _ ≤ m ^ 2 * (R * ((m ^ (alpha / 2))⁻¹ * gradEnergy φ ^ (alpha / 2))) :=
   372	          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 hm2.le
   373	      _ = R * (m ^ 2 / m ^ (alpha / 2) * gradEnergy φ ^ (alpha / 2)) := by
   374	          field_simp

   376	/-- The smooth square bound (TeX lines 186-189): for real `φ, ψ ∈ C_c^∞`, a locally finite even `Γ`

     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}

    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.

    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{lemma}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  Choose nonnegative nonzero $f \in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ and $s_0 = 1/2$. Let
    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.
    65	
    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]
    73	  Extend $f_n$ by zero. It is smooth compact, vanishes near both endpoints, is
    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.
    82	
    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.
    86	  \]
    87	  Its time integrand increases to $f_a$, so the cost tends to
    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.
    91	  Such a ball exists by exhaustion. Take the limit of the individual
    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves
    95	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
    99	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   100	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   101	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   102	  a positive finite real number, and
   103	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   104	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   105	    k\left[
   106	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   107	    \right]^{1/k}.
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	\end{proposition}
   110	
   111	\begin{proof}
   112	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero
   113	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   114	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   115	  autocorrelation argument in the preceding proof gives $0 < A: =
   116	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) < \infty$. With $U_\ell g(x) = \ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the
   117	  physical changes of variables give
   118	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   119	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   120	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   121	  \end{equation}
   122	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   123	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   124	
   125	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   126	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   127	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   128	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   129	  \[
   130	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   131	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   132	  \]
   133	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   134	  gives
   135	  \[
   136	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   137	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   138	  \]
   139	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   140	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   141	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. The already finite
   142	  $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ bounds every ratio by
   143	  $8M_aq^{q/2}(S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}/k)^k/\alpha^{\alpha/2}$. A normalized compact
   144	  bump supplies a positive ratio. This proves positivity and finiteness of $R_0$
   145	  before any rough spatial extension is invoked. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   147	\end{proof}

   149	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   150	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   151	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   152	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   153	  \begin{align}
   154	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   155	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   156	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   157	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   158	  \end{align}
   159	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   160	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   161	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   162	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   163	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   164	  \end{equation}
   165	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   166	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   167	\end{proposition}
   168	
   169	\begin{proof}
   170	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   171	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   172	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   173	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   174	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   175	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   176	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   177	  convention gives
   178	  \[
   179	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   180	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   181	  \]
   182	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   183	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   184	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   185	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   186	  \[
   187	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   188	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   189	  \]
   190	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   191	
   192	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   193	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   194	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   195	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   196	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   197	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   198	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   199	
   200	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   201	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   202	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   203	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   204	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   205	  continuity.
   206	
   207	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   208	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   209	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   210	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   211	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   212	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   213	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   214	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   215	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   216	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   217	
   218	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   219	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   220	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   221	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   222	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   223	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   224	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   225	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   226	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   227	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   228	\end{proof}

   230	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   231	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   232	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   233	  \[
   234	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   235	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   236	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   237	  \]
   238	  Then
   239	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   240	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   241	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   242	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   243	    \in(0,\infty).
   244	  \end{equation}
   245	  In particular,
   246	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   247	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   248	    \qquad
   249	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   250	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   251	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   252	  \end{equation}
   253	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   254	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   255	\end{proposition}
   256	
   257	\begin{proof}
   258	  Physical change of variables, or smooth approximation and
   259	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, extends \eqref{E:spatial-dilation} to
   260	  real $H^1$ profiles. For fixed unit $g$, with $A,b > 0$, the maximum of
   261	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals
   262	  \[
   263	    \frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   264	    R(g)^{2/(2-\alpha)}.
   265	  \]
   266	  Dilation preserves the whole unit class and includes $\ell = 1$. Taking both
   267	  numerical suprema, then profiles with ratio tending to $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$,
   268	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. No optimizer is assumed. Smooth ratios
   269	  also approach $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   270	  Pass them through~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score} and substitute
   271	  \[
   272	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}\alpha^{\alpha/2}
   273	    =\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2-\alpha}
   274	    \right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}.
   275	  \]
   276	  This gives~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. This proves
   277	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-energy-map}.
   278	\end{proof}

   280	\subsection{The kernel row and full occupation energy}
   281	
   282	Define, for $u \ne 0$,
   283	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-damped-kernel}
   284	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}
   285	  \int_0^\infty
   286	  e^{-(\lambda+\lambda^2/(2D))|u|}
   287	  \lambda^{a-1}\ud\lambda,
   288	\end{equation}
   289	and set $K_\star(0) = 0$ for time integration.
   290	
   291	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   292	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   293	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   294	  $[0,1]$ is
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   296	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t
   297	    =R_\star:=2\int_0^{1/2}K_\star(u)\ud u\in(0,\infty).
   298	  \end{equation}
   299	\end{lemma}
   300	
   301	\begin{proof}
   302	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   303	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   304	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   305	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   306	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   307	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   308	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   309	\end{proof}
   310	
   311	Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the full class of strongly $H^1(\R^d;\R)$-measurable fields
   312	$s\mapsto g_s$ on $(0,1)$ with $\|g_s\|_2 = 1$ a.e. and $T(g) =
   313	\int_0^1b(g_s)\ud s < \infty$. No time smoothness, common compact support or
   314	optimizer condition is imposed.
   315	
   316	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   317	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   318	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   319	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   320	  \[
   321	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1
   322	    K_\star(s-t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,
   323	  \]
   324	  every $g \in \mathcal{O}$ satisfies
   325	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   326	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   327	  \end{equation}
   328	  The energy over exactly this full class satisfies
   329	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   330	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   331	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)
   332	    \le R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty.
   333	  \end{equation}
   334	\end{proposition}
   335	
   336	\begin{proof}
   337	  The map $s\mapsto b(g_s)$ is measurable by continuity of the squared gradient
   338	  norm. Also $\int_0^1\|g_s\|_{H^1}^2\ud s = 1+T(g)$. Use a separably valued
   339	  strong representative and replace exceptional null times by one fixed real
   340	  unit compact bump. Joint measurable spatial representatives exist: approximate
   341	  this Bochner $L^2$ field by simple $H^1$-valued functions with summable
   342	  $L^2(0,1;H^1)$ errors, and choose measurable spatial versions for their
   343	  countably many values. A subsequence has a measurable spacetime $L^2$ limit,
   344	  and for a.e. $s$ its spatial $L^2$ class is $g_s$.
   345	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair} makes every pairing independent of the
   346	  spatial versions. The continuous pairing map on the separable space $H^1\times
   347	  H^1$ from Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} consequently gives a
   348	  measurable function of $(s,t)$ agreeing a.e. with the nonnegative physical
   349	  integral.
   350	
   351	  Set $F(s) = b(g_s)^{\alpha/4}$. Equations~\eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}
   352	  and~\eqref{E:spatial-square-CS} give $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   353	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}F(s)F(t)$. Since $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$, concavity on the unit time
   354	  interval yields $\int_0^1F^2 = \int_0^1b(g_s)^{\alpha/2}\ud s \le
   355	  T(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Now use $2F(s)F(t) \le F(s)^2+F(t)^2$ and the exact row
   356	  bound \eqref{E:occupation-kernel-row}, whose column bound is the same because
   357	  $K_\star$ is even, to obtain \eqref{E:occupation-physical-bound}. Positive
   358	  Tonelli is valid before finiteness is known. Null-time modifications affect
   359	  only a product-null set, so they cannot change $J$.
   360	
   361	  The scalar maximum of $R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T^{\alpha/2}-T/2$ over $T \ge 0$
   362	  is $R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$, by the same
   363	  differentiation as~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. This bounds the occupation
   364	  supremum from above. For positivity take a constant-in-time unit compact
   365	  profile and its spatial dilation $U_\ell$. Its $J$ is $J_0\ell^\alpha
   366	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)$, where $J_0 = \int_0^1\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud s\ud t \in
   367	  (0,\infty)$, while $T = \ell^2b(g)$. For sufficiently small $\ell > 0$,

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}

   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
